sentences.text: Eoscyllium is interpreted as a carpet shark, probably belonging to the family Hemiscylliidae.
Fossils of Eoscyllium have been found in Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, and the United Kingdom.
In the Paleobiology Database, Eoscyllium is listed as a genus authored by Delsate in 2026.
Twelve fossil occurrences of Eoscyllium have been recorded in the database.
The genus Eoscyllium is considered valid.
The type species of Eoscyllium is the previously named "Heterodontus" duffini described by Thies in 1983.
Eoscyllium is placed within the family Hemiscylliidae.
Eoscyllium belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Eoscyllium lived during the Jurassic period, specifically from the Toarcian to the Kimmeridgian ages.
Its temporal range extends from the Toarcian to the Tithonian, about 182.9 to 145.06 million years ago.
